# Quantum Group Escape

This repository studies full random-unitary channel simulation from an unknown unitary representation of a known finite group. With at most q generator calls, its dimension-uniform minimax unhalved diamond error is twice the probability that the endpoint has word length greater than q. Under classical stopping, the optimum expected count is the sum of the word-length tails trimmed by half the error allowance. A four-generator nonabelian wreath family has three-quarter-power hard-query scaling along growing finite quotients.

- Integer-lamp wreath group, exact line word length, conditional Skellam lamps, cursor occupation times and finite high escape quantiles: science/wreath-product.md
- Explicit finite groups, kernel/metric-ball proof, Poisson coupling, asymptotic finite-family query law and target width: science/finite-quotients.md
- Capped sampler, finite probability precision, query execution order, direct normal form, classical storage and physical oracle cost: science/algorithms-and-resources.md

- Earlier group twirls, stable Hamiltonian twirls, accessible-gate depth, reflection word compression, classical escape and parity: references/related-work.md
- Reproducible exact finite relations/gauge checks and floating channel diagnostics: verification/README.md and verification/check_finite_groups.py

## Preserve these distinctions

- The exact hard cap is the upper escape quantile at epsilon/2. With classical stopping, longest-distance trimming attains all optimal count tails at once. At zero error its expected count equals the mean escape distance.
- The representation is unknown and available through generator calls. The group relations are exact. A classical matrix description or richer arbitrary-power access changes the model.
- A hard cap holds on every branch. The expected guarantee is uniform over representations and inputs and uses a classically observed stopping count. A controlled call counts once even if a coherent component idles.
- The example's finite group and hard representation dimension grow with time. No fixed-dimension long-time power law is claimed.
- The direct endpoint sampler has linear classical event work. Oracle-call fast forwarding does not establish an end-to-end runtime advantage.
- Intermediate simulation exponents, group twirling and the classical wreath escape exponent have earlier sources. The added statement concerns representation-uniform generator-query optimality from group geometry.
- The output is the reduced CPTP system channel, including arbitrary reference inputs. A specified coherent bath or jump record is a different task.
